newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: LatAm shrs seen mixed - some wobbly, Brazil rising.
newsitem.headline: LatAm shrs seen mixed - some wobbly, Brazil rising.

text.p: Third quarter earnings reports, political scandals and macroeconomic fundamentals were seen taking Latin American stock markets in mixed and varied directions, traders and analysts said, with no overall regional trend.

Argentine stocks were seen glued to the ups and downs of the government's corruption scandal. Mexican and Chilean markets will be watching for surprises amid a slew of earnings reports. And Venezuela is seen treading water on a dearth of news on the long-awaited privatization of phone company CANTV.

Only Brazilian shares look robust against this back drop, analysts say. Options expiration is expected to clear the way for foreign investors to return to telecom, power and retail sector shares with the index expected to rally in heavy trade on top of last week's 2.87 percent gain.

In Argentina, a lack of new data has left traders divided on the effects of a continuing political row that has pitted former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo against key government ministers. Last week, Cavallo accused the ministers of covering up corruption cases and manipulating judges, forcing President Carlos Menem to come out in defense of his cabinet.

"I'd say the market ended on a firm note Friday because it recouped significant losses and digested the political news," said Rafael Aldazabal of Aldazabal brokers. The blue-chip MerVal index recovered towards the end of last week, but still closed off 2.5 percent at 569.65.

After a near vertical rise in early October, Venezuelan shares are seen pausing for breath as investors await greater details of the government's privatization plans before taking the bolsa to new highs.
"Now's a good time to be taking positions," said Carlos Lupini of Incambios brokers. "Interest rates are low and liquidity high."
Last week the 19-share index slipped 3.4 percent to close at 5,757.86 points.
In Mexico, peso stability and strong corporate results are seen gently firming stocks.
"We feel the market ... may pause occasionally, but will climb towards a short term objective of 3,410 points," said Estrategia brokerage research director Roberto Solano.
Meanwhile Chilean stock watchers will be zeroing in on a possible cut of electricity generating prices ahead of a government review due to be published in November.

Government follow-up on the surprise failure last week to privatize electricity company Colbun Machicura SA will further spotlight power shares, which account for 40 percent of the weighting in the 40-share IPSA index.
The index slipped 0.6 percent in the week to end at 101.58 points.
